questions.stem:
The stem lengths of a sample of 120 tulips are recorded in the grouped frequency table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Stem length (cm)} & \text{Frequency}\\ \hline 40 \leqslant x < 42 & 12\\ \hline 42 \leqslant x < 45 & 18\\ \hline 45 \leqslant x < 50 & 23\\ \hline 50 \leqslant x < 55 & 35\\ \hline 55 \leqslant x < 58 & 24\\ \hline 58 \leqslant x < 60 & 8\\ \hline\end{array}$

A histogram is drawn to represent these data.

The area of the bar representing the $40 \leqslant x < 42$ class is $16.5\,\text{cm}^2$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Calculate the exact area of the bar representing the $42 \leqslant x < 45$ class.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: [Area $= k \times$ frequency $\rightarrow 16.5 = k \times 12 \rightarrow$] Area $= \frac{16.5}{12} \times 18$ oe
A1: $= 24.75\,(\text{cm}^2)$
M1 allow equivalent eg $16.5 \times \frac{3}{2}$
A1 for 24.75; allow 24.8

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The height of the tallest bar in the histogram is $10\,\text{cm}$.

(b) Find the exact height of the second tallest bar.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: fd method $\frac{24}{58-55}[=8]$ and $\frac{35}{55-50}[=7]$ or Area method $\frac{16.5}{12}\times 24[=33]$ and $\frac{16.5}{12}\times 35[=48.125]$ or $\frac{16.5}{12}\times \frac{24}{3}[=11]$ and $\frac{16.5}{12}\times \frac{35}{5}[=9.625]$
Let h = height of the 2nd tallest bar
dM1: $[h=]\frac{10}{8}\times 7$ or $[h=]\text{`48.125'}\times \frac{10\times 3}{5\times \text{`33'}}$ or $[h=]\text{`9.625'}\times \frac{10}{\text{`11'}}$
A1: $= 8.75\,(\text{cm})$
M1: correct method for finding the frequency density or area for the highest and 2nd highest bars. Allow if 8 and 7 seen or 33 and 48.125 seen or 9.625 rather than 48.125 and/or 11 seen rather than 33
dM1: dep on previous M mark awarded. A fully correct expression for h or a fully correct equation to enable h to be found eg $\frac{\text{`33'}}{10\times 3}=\frac{\text{`48.125'}}{5h}$
A1: 8.75 oe. NB answer of 8.75 seen as final answer 3/3

parts.label: c
parts.text:
$Q_1$ for these data is $45\,\text{cm}$.

(c) Use linear interpolation to find an estimate for

(i) $Q_2$

(ii) the interquartile range.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(i) M1: $[Q_2=]50+\frac{7}{35}\times 5$ or $[Q_2=]55-\frac{28}{35}\times 5$
A1: $= 51\,(\text{cm})$
M1 for $50+\frac{7}{35}\times k$ or $55-\frac{28}{35}\times k$ or $\frac{Q_2-50}{k}=\frac{60-53}{88-53}$ or $\frac{55-Q_2}{k}=\frac{88-60}{88-53}$ where $4 \leqslant k \leqslant 6$ oe (condone use of $n+1$ ie 7.5 rather than 7, 27.5 rather than 28 or 60.5 rather than 60)
A1: 51 (condone for use of $n+1$ awrt 51.1)
(ii) M1: $[Q_3=]55+\frac{2}{24}\times 3$ or $[Q_3=]58-\frac{22}{24}\times 3$ and "55.25" $-45$
A1: $= 10.25\,(\text{cm})$
M1: $55+\frac{2}{24}\times t$ or $58-\frac{22}{24}\times t$ or $\frac{Q_3-55}{t}=\frac{90-88}{112-88}$ or $\frac{58-Q_3}{t}=\frac{112-90}{112-88}$ oe where $2 \leqslant t \leqslant 4$ and using "their $Q_3$" $-45$ (condone use of $n+1$ ie 2.5 or 2.75 rather than 2, 21.5 or 21.25 rather than 22 or 90.5 or 90.75 rather than 90)
A1: 10.25 oe eg 41/4; allow 10.3 from correct working

parts.label: d
parts.text:
One measure of skewness is given by

$\frac{Q_3-2Q_2+Q_1}{Q_3-Q_1}$

(d) By calculating this measure, describe the skewness of these data.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: $\frac{\text{"55.25"}-2(\text{"51"})+45}{\text{"55.25"}-45}$
A1ft: $[=-0.17073\ldots < 0]$ negative [skew].
M1: substitution of their values from (c) seen or awrt $-0.17$ or $-7/41$
A1ft: dependent on M1 being scored. Correct description of skewness consistent with their values from part (c); ignore the final answer if working shown. Only allow no skew or symmetrical if their value should be 0. Ignore correlation.

questions.stem:
Morgan is investigating the body length, $b$ centimetres, of squirrels.

A random sample of 8 squirrels is taken and the data for each squirrel is coded using

$x = \frac{b-21}{2}$

The results for the coded data are summarised below

$\sum x = -1.2 \qquad \sum x^2 = 5.1$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: $[\bar{x}=]\frac{-1.2}{8}[=-0.15]$
M1: "$-0.15$" $=\frac{\bar{b}-21}{2}$ oe
A1: $=20.7\,(\text{cm})$
1st M1 for correct expression for $\bar{x}$, ignore letter (or 1st M1 for correct expression for $\sum b$: $\sum b = 21\times 8+2\times(-1.2)[=165.6]$)
2nd M1: Using equation. "$\bar{x}$" $=\frac{\bar{b}-21}{2}$ where $-1.2 <$ '$\bar{x}$' $< 1.2$; condone b rather than $\bar{b}$ (or 2nd M1: use of "$\sum b$" $\div n$ where '$\sum b$' $>18$: $[\bar{b}=]\frac{165.6}{8}$)
A1: 20.7 oe

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $\sigma_x=\sqrt{\frac{5.1}{8}-\left(\frac{-1.2}{8}\right)^2}[=\sqrt{0.615}=0.784\ldots]$
M1: $\sigma_b=2\times$ '0.784...'
A1: $=$ awrt $1.57\,(\text{cm})$
1st M1: correct method for $\sigma_x$ or $\sigma_x^2$ or $5.1=\frac{\sum b^2-42\times\text{"168.6"}+8\times 441}{4}$ or $\sum b^2=3447.6$
2nd M1: for use of $2\times$ their $\sigma_x$ (or $4\times$ their $\sigma_x^2$) (adding 21 is M0) or $\frac{\text{"3447.6"}}{8}-\left(\frac{\text{"165.6"}}{8}\right)^2$ or $\sqrt{\frac{\text{"3447.6"}}{8}-\left(\frac{\text{"165.6"}}{8}\right)^2}$
A1: awrt 1.57. Allow $\frac{\sqrt{246}}{10}$ (allow $s_b=$ awrt 1.68 or $\frac{4\sqrt{246}}{35}$ from an $n-1$ method)

parts.label: c(i)
parts.text:
A 9th squirrel is added to the sample. Given that for all 9 squirrels $\sum x = 0$

(c) find

(i) the body length of the 9th squirrel,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(i) M1: $x_9=1.2 \rightarrow b_9=1.2\times 2+21$ oe or $9\times 21-8\times$'20.7'$[=354.6]$
A1: $=23.4\,(\text{cm})$
M1: for a correct equation using $x_9=1.2$ to enable $b_9$ to be found eg $1.2=\frac{b-21}{2}$ or a correct method to find $\sum x$ for the 9 squirrels; ft their 20.7
A1: 23.4 oe

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.text:
(ii) the standard deviation of $x$ for all 9 squirrels.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(ii) M1: $\sum x^2=5.1+1.2^2[=6.54] \Rightarrow \sigma_x=\sqrt{\frac{5.1+1.2^2}{9}-0^2}$
A1: $=$ awrt $0.852\,(\text{cm})$
M1: for $5.1+\text{"}(\pm 1.2)\text{"}^2[=6.54]$ seen ft their $x_9$; condone $5.1+(\pm 9.6)^2[=97.26]$
A1: awrt 0.852; allow $\frac{\sqrt{654}}{30}$ (allow $s_x=$ awrt 0.904 from an $n-1$ method)

questions.stem:
The weights, $W$ grams, of kiwi fruit grown on a farm are normally distributed with mean 80 grams and standard deviation 8 grams.

The table shows the classifications of the kiwi fruit by their weight, where $k$ is a positive constant.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Small (Tiny)} & \text{Small (Petite)} & \text{Large (Extra)} & \text{Large (Jumbo)} & \text{Large (Mega)}\\ \hline w<66 & 66 \leqslant w<70 & 70 \leqslant w<80 & 80 \leqslant w<k & w \geqslant k\\ \hline\end{array}$

One kiwi fruit is selected at random from those grown on the farm.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that this kiwi fruit is Large.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: $\mathrm{P}(W>70)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{70-80}{8}[=-1.25]\right)$
A1: $=\mathrm{P}(Z>-1.25)$ or $\mathrm{P}(Z<1.25)$
A1: $=0.8944$; awrt 0.894
M1: for standardising with 70, 80 and 8 (allow $\pm$)
1st A1: $z=\pm 1.25$
2nd A1: awrt 0.894 (calc 0.894350...) NB do not ISW so an answer of 0.1056 is A0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
35% of the kiwi fruit are Jumbo.

(b) Find the value of $k$ to one decimal place.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: $\mathrm{P}(W<k)=0.85$ or $\mathrm{P}(W>k)=0.15$
M1, B1: $\pm\left(\frac{k-80}{8}\right)=1.0364$
A1: $k=88.29\ldots$; awrt 88.3
1st B1: for either correct probability statement. Allow $\leqslant$ for $<$ and $\geqslant$ for $>$ (may be implied by $z=$ awrt 1.04)
M1: standardising with 80, 8 and equating to $z$, where $1<|z|<2$
2nd B1: $z=\pm 1.0364$ or better (calc 1.036432...)
A1: awrt 88.3 (calc 88.291459...). NB awrt 88.3 implies 1st B1 and M1 but not the 2nd B1; they could get B1M1B0A1 (Answer only 88.291 to 88.292 scored 4 out of 4)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
75% of Tiny kiwi fruit weigh more than $y$ grams.

(c) Find the value of $y$ giving your answer to one decimal place.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $\mathrm{P}(W<66)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{66-80}{8}[=-1.75]\right)[=0.0401\,(\text{calc } 0.040059\ldots)]$
dM1: $0.25\times\mathrm{P}(Z<-1.75)[=0.010025\,(\text{calc } 0.0100147\ldots)]$ or $0.25\times(1-\mathrm{P}(Z<1.75))$
M1, A1: $\frac{y-80}{8}=-2.32(63)$
A1: $y=61.389\ldots$; awrt 61.4
1st M1: standardising with 66, 80 and 8 (allow $\pm$) or seeing awrt 0.0401 in working
2nd dM1: dep on 1st M1; $0.25\times$ "their $\mathrm{P}(Z<-1.75)$" or $0.0401-0.030075$ or seeing $[0.75\times 0.0401+0.9599=]0.9899\ldots$
3rd M1: for standardising and equating to $z$, where $|z|>2$
1st A1: correct standardisation equation with compatible signs and $2.32 \leqslant |z| \leqslant 2.34$
2nd A1: awrt 61.4 (allow awrt 61.3)

questions.stem:
The Venn diagram shows the events $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$, where $p$, $q$, $r$ and $s$ are probabilities.

[Venn diagram: circle $A$ contains 0.13 outside circle $B$ which contains 0.12; separately circle $C$ contains region $p$ (outside overlap) and overlaps circle $D$ in region $q$; circle $D$ contains region $r$ outside the overlap and $s$ is outside both $C$ and $D$.]

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a)(i) B1: 0.25 oe
(ii) B1: 1 cao
(iii) B1: 0 cao

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that $\mathrm{P}(B' \cap D')=\frac{7}{10}$ and $\mathrm{P}(C|D)=\frac{3}{5}$

(b) find the exact value of $q$ and the exact value of $r$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $\frac{q}{q+r}=\frac{3}{5}$
M1: $0.13+p+s=\frac{7}{10}$
M1: $p+q+r+s+0.12+0.13=1$
Solving simultaneously to get
dM1: $\frac{q}{0.3-0.12}=\frac{3}{5}$ or $0.3=0.12+1.5r+r$ or $0.3=0.12+q+\frac{2}{3}q$ oe
A1: $q=0.108$
A1: $r=0.072$
1st M1: correct expression for $\mathrm{P}(C|D)=\frac{3}{5}$. Allow $\mathrm{P}(D)$ for $q+r$
2nd M1: correct expression for $\mathrm{P}(B' \cap D')=\frac{7}{10}$
3rd M1: a correct equation or use of sum of probabilities = 1; must imply correct equation eg may ft their $\mathrm{P}(B' \cap D')=\frac{7}{10}$. Implied by $q+r=0.18$ or $\mathrm{P}(D)=0.18$ [NB: $\frac{3}{10}=0.12+q+r$ is 2nd M1 3rd M1]
4th dM1: dep on all 3 previous M1 being awarded; solving to obtain a correct equation in a single variable. Implied by a correct value for $q$ or $r$
1st A1: $q=0.108$ or $\frac{27}{250}$ oe
2nd A1: $r=0.072$ or $\frac{9}{125}$ oe

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given also that $\mathrm{P}(B \cup C')=\frac{5}{8}$

(c) find the exact value of $s$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $\frac{5}{8}=0.13+0.12+\text{'0.072'}+s$ oe
A1: $s=0.303$
M1: correct expression for $\mathrm{P}(B \cup C')=\frac{5}{8}$ ft their value for $r$. Allow use of the letter $r$ eg $\frac{5}{8}=0.13+0.12+r+s$ oe. We will condone values of $r$ outside the range $0<r<1$
A1: $s=0.303$ oe

questions.question_text:
The Venn diagram shows the events $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$, where $p$, $q$, $r$ and $s$ are probabilities.

[Venn diagram: circle $A$ contains 0.13 outside circle $B$ which contains 0.12; separately circle $C$ contains region $p$ (outside overlap) and overlaps circle $D$ in region $q$; circle $D$ contains region $r$ outside the overlap and $s$ is outside both $C$ and $D$.]
(a) Write down the value of

(i) $\mathrm{P}(A)$

(ii) $\mathrm{P}(A|B)$

(iii) $\mathrm{P}(A|C)$
(3)
Given that $\mathrm{P}(B' \cap D')=\frac{7}{10}$ and $\mathrm{P}(C|D)=\frac{3}{5}$

(b) find the exact value of $q$ and the exact value of $r$
(6)
Given also that $\mathrm{P}(B \cup C')=\frac{5}{8}$

(c) find the exact value of $s$
(2)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a)(i) B1: 0.25 oe
(ii) B1: 1 cao
(iii) B1: 0 cao
(b) M1: $\frac{q}{q+r}=\frac{3}{5}$
M1: $0.13+p+s=\frac{7}{10}$
M1: $p+q+r+s+0.12+0.13=1$
Solving simultaneously to get
dM1: $\frac{q}{0.3-0.12}=\frac{3}{5}$ or $0.3=0.12+1.5r+r$ or $0.3=0.12+q+\frac{2}{3}q$ oe
A1: $q=0.108$
A1: $r=0.072$
1st M1: correct expression for $\mathrm{P}(C|D)=\frac{3}{5}$. Allow $\mathrm{P}(D)$ for $q+r$
2nd M1: correct expression for $\mathrm{P}(B' \cap D')=\frac{7}{10}$
3rd M1: a correct equation or use of sum of probabilities = 1; must imply correct equation eg may ft their $\mathrm{P}(B' \cap D')=\frac{7}{10}$. Implied by $q+r=0.18$ or $\mathrm{P}(D)=0.18$ [NB: $\frac{3}{10}=0.12+q+r$ is 2nd M1 3rd M1]
4th dM1: dep on all 3 previous M1 being awarded; solving to obtain a correct equation in a single variable. Implied by a correct value for $q$ or $r$
1st A1: $q=0.108$ or $\frac{27}{250}$ oe
2nd A1: $r=0.072$ or $\frac{9}{125}$ oe
(c) M1: $\frac{5}{8}=0.13+0.12+\text{'0.072'}+s$ oe
A1: $s=0.303$
M1: correct expression for $\mathrm{P}(B \cup C')=\frac{5}{8}$ ft their value for $r$. Allow use of the letter $r$ eg $\frac{5}{8}=0.13+0.12+r+s$ oe. We will condone values of $r$ outside the range $0<r<1$
A1: $s=0.303$ oe
